title: The Blue Chip USDT vault appears in the Artifact twice, as a completed capital allocation and as a live curation mandate
content:
The Spark Blue Chip USDT Morpho Vault (A.6.1.1.1.3.9.7.2.3) has contract address `0xc7CDcFDEfC64631ED6799C95e3b110cd42F2bD22`. That is the same address recorded as the token address of the Ethereum Mainnet Morpho USDT Instance under **Completed Instances** of the Spark Liquidity Layer (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.4.3.1.1.2.2.1), whose Curator and Guardian role addresses (.4.2.1, .4.2.2) are also the identical Soter Labs and Spark Foundation safes.

One contract, two sections of the Artifact, two different statuses. It is not a contradiction — it is two different relationships to the same vault, and separating them is the useful insight:

- Under the **Allocation System Primitive**, the question is whether *Spark's own capital* is deployed into that vault. `Completed` means that allocation has been wound up.
- Under the **Risk Curation Framework**, the question is whether Spark holds and exercises admin authority over the vault on behalf of *third-party depositors*. That mandate is live.

Spark can therefore have fully exited a vault as an investor while remaining responsible for curating it as an operator — and the second obligation is the more consequential one, because other people's money is still inside.

The structural lesson is that the Artifact's status fields are scoped to their framework, not to the asset. Reading only the Allocation System tree would show a completed, closed-out position; reading only the Risk Curation tree would show an active mandate with no indication that Spark's own capital has left. Neither view is wrong and neither is sufficient, and nothing in either section cross-references the other.

For anyone auditing Spark's real obligations, this means enumerating by contract address across frameworks rather than by section — the same discipline the two duplicated Encumbrance Ratio entries require for parameters.
